title: Souvenir — Fogg's notebook, and yours
learning_goal: Take away the seven lines with a blank column beside them, and one train that can still be booked; feel quiet satisfaction at having stopped where Fogg did not.

narration.script:
Six days from here, at Suez, Fogg finds he is exactly on time. Then Verne writes the sharpest sentence in the book about him. Fogg eats breakfast in his cabin and never thinks of looking at the town — 'one of those Englishmen who are wont to see foreign countries through the eyes of their domestics.'

Your souvenir is his notebook: seven lines, three thousand kilometres, an empty column headed 'what I saw'. On the back, the one thing you can still book: Paris to Turin, through Sommeiller's tunnel.

media.note: SPEC (G-208, state b) — PRINTABLE. RIGHT-HAND COLUMN EMPTY, headed 'what I saw'. Time style '8:45 pm' per R1; dates 'Saturday 5 October 1872'. ON THE BACK: 'Paris to Turin, still through the Fréjus tunnel. Closed by a rockfall for nineteen months; reopened 31 March 2025.' and one line under it: 'Sommeiller's tunnel, 154 years old, and still the way through.' Typeset from G-204's newspaper style.
